raw_case_text:
A 57-year-old previously healthy Caucasian male presented to a community hospital with a 3-day onset of epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and new-onset ascites. Initial workup revealed normal liver function studies. His lipase was elevated. Diagnostic paracentesis was consistent with hemorrhagic fluid with red blood cell count of 640 504/mm3 and white blood cell count of 1440/mm3. Computed tomography scan of the abdomen was concerning for a 15 mm lesion in the pancreatic head, peripancreatic stranding, and large-volume ascites. He was transferred to this tertiary care hospital for further workup of acute hemorrhagic pancreatitis and possible endoscopic ultrasound/endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography for further workup of the pancreatic head lesion.
He had been in good health prior to this presentation. Past medical history was pertinent for hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. He had no history of pancreatitis, gallstones, or other hepatobiliary disease. Social history revealed that he was active, independent, and lived by himself. He had 1 rum drink daily and smoked 2 cigarettes per day. Review of systems was pertinent for blistering of the hands, with subsequent scabbing and pigmentation changes, with onset a few days prior to the abdominal pain. He was not sure if there was a relationship to sun exposure. Associated with the blisters, the patient described unrelenting pruritis of his hands bilaterally. This was the first time in his life he was experiencing cutaneous symptoms as he had never had skin problems before.
On admission to our institution, vital signs demonstrated temperature 37.0 C, blood pressure 146/95 mm Hg, heart rate 112 beats per minute, respiratory rate 20 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. On examination, he was in mild distress from abdominal pain and nausea. Abdomen was distended and mildly tender in the epigastric region. A fluid wave was appreciated. There was no hepatosplenomegaly. Dermatology examination revealed vesicles and bullae with erythematous bases, in different stages of healing seen over the dorsal aspects of the both hands with scaling, scarring, and hypopigmentation and hyperpigmentation of the skin (Figure 1). They were pruritic but not painful. There was no hypertrichosis appreciated. There were no stigmata of chronic liver disease and no scleral icterus.
Complete blood count demonstrated hemoglobin of 8.5 gm/dL (mean corpuscular volume 95 fL), white blood cell count of 10 500/mm3 (76% polymorphonuclear cells), and platelets 328 000/mm3. Renal function tests were normal. Liver function tests demonstrated total bilirubin 0.3 mg/dL, aspartate aminotransferase 16 U/L, alanine aminotransferase 7 U/L, alkaline phosphatase 88 U/L, and albumin 1.6 g/dL. The international normalized ratio was 1.35. Lipase was elevated to 352 U/L. Repeat diagnostic paracentesis again demonstrated grossly bloody fluid with an amylase of 2866 U/L.
Further workup for acute hemorrhagic pancreatitis included a computed tomography angiogram, which did not show active bleeding. The nature of the pancreatic head lesion was still indeterminate so an endoscopic ultrasound was performed, which did not show any focal lesion concerning for malignancy. Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography done showed a large proximal pancreatic duct disruption, which was treated with a plastic stent. He was managed supportively with intravenous fluids and pain relief for acute hemorrhagic pancreatitis.
Further workup of his skin lesions was initiated due to the concern for porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT). Skin biopsy showed blistering dermatosis, subepithelial with evidence of re-epithelialization. Periodic acid-Schiff stain (PAS) with diastase highlighted increased PAS+ deposition around vessel walls and focal PAS+ deposits within the epidermis (Figure 2). Direct immunofluorescence demonstrated homogenously thickened dermal blood vessels highlighted by immunoglobulin (Ig)G, IgA, C1q, fibrin, kappa, and lambda. The specimen was negative for deposition of IgM and C3. Findings were consistent with PCT. Serum porphyrin levels came back strongly positive with levels of 8 microg% (upper limit of normal <0.9 microg%). Fractionation revealed high heptacarboxyl, hexacarboxyl, and pentacarboxyl porphyrins as expected with the heptacarboxyl highest at 2.6 microg% and the other 2 at 1.4 microg% each. After confirmation of the diagnosis, hepatitis C, hepatitis B, and HIV were ordered and returned negative.
Unfortunately, our patient developed secondary bacterial peritonitis and quickly deteriorated. His repeat ascitic fluid grew Candida and Enterococcus. His respiratory status declined as he developed acute respiratory distress syndrome and needed mechanical ventilation. He then progressed to multiorgan failure a few days later and eventually died.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 57-year-old Caucasian male presented with a 3-day history of epigastric abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, and new-onset hemorrhagic ascites preceded by a several-day history of intensely pruritic blistering lesions on the dorsal hands.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Several days prior to the onset of abdominal pain, the patient developed intensely pruritic vesicles, bullae, scabbing, and pigmentary changes over the dorsal aspects of both hands for the first time in his life. Three days prior to community hospital presentation, he developed acute epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, and large-volume hemorrhagic ascites with an elevated lipase and a 15 mm pancreatic head abnormality on CT, prompting tertiary transfer.
subjective.past_medical_history: Hypertension and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD); no prior history of pancreatitis, cholelithiasis, liver disease, or skin disorders. Social history notable for 1 rum drink daily and smoking 2 cigarettes per day.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for epigastric pain, nausea, vomiting, abdominal distension, and severe bilateral dorsal hand pruritus and blistering.

objective.physical_examination: Admission vital signs: temperature 37.0 °C, blood pressure 146/95 mmHg, heart rate 112 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, and SpO2 96% on room air. Abdominal examination showed distension, mild epigastric tenderness, and a positive fluid wave without hepatosplenomegaly, scleral icterus, or chronic liver stigmata. Dermatological examination revealed pruritic, painless vesicles and bullae on erythematous bases in varying stages of healing with scaling, scarring, and hypo-/hyperpigmentation over the dorsal aspects of both hands without hypertrichosis.
objective.routine_investigations: Labs showed normocytic anemia (hemoglobin 8.5 g/dL, MCV 95 fL), WBC 10,500/mm3 (76% PMNs), platelets 328,000/mm3, normal renal function, normal transaminases and bilirubin (total bilirubin 0.3 mg/dL, AST 16 U/L, ALT 7 U/L, ALP 88 U/L), severe hypoalbuminemia (1.6 g/dL), INR 1.35, and elevated serum lipase (352 U/L). Diagnostic paracentesis yielded grossly hemorrhagic ascitic fluid (RBC 640,504/mm3, WBC 1,440/mm3) with markedly elevated ascitic amylase (2,866 U/L), and repeat ascitic fluid culture later grew Candida and Enterococcus. Total serum porphyrins were markedly elevated at 8 µg% (normal <0.9 µg%) with elevated heptacarboxyl (2.6 µg%), hexacarboxyl (1.4 µg%), and pentacarboxyl (1.4 µg%) porphyrins. Hepatitis B, hepatitis C, and HIV serologies were all negative.
objective.advanced_workup: Abdominal CT showed a 15 mm pancreatic head lesion, peripancreatic fat stranding, and large-volume ascites; CT angiography showed no active arterial hemorrhage; endoscopic ultrasound (EUS) excluded pancreatic malignancy; and ERCP identified a large proximal main pancreatic duct disruption that was bridged with a plastic pancreatic stent. Dorsal hand skin biopsy with PAS-diastase and direct immunofluorescence (DIF) demonstrated a subepidermal pauci-inflammatory blister with re-epithelialization and homogeneous perivascular and dermoepidermal PAS-positive and IgG, IgA, C1q, fibrin, kappa, and lambda deposition diagnostic of porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: New-onset sporadic porphyria cutanea tarda (PCT, confirmed by subepidermal blister histopathology, perivascular PAS/DIF deposition, and elevated serum heptacarboxyl/hexacarboxyl/pentacarboxyl porphyrins of 8 µg% with negative HIV, HBV, and HCV testing) co-occurring with severe acute hemorrhagic/pancreatic-ascites pancreatitis secondary to proximal main pancreatic duct disruption. Despite ERCP pancreatic duct stenting and supportive care, the patient's hemorrhagic pancreatic ascites became superinfected with Candida and Enterococcus (secondary fungal/bacterial peritonitis), and he progressed to ARDS requiring mechanical ventilation, multiorgan failure, and death.
